statement.text: A graph ''G'' is said to be a '''Seymour graph''' if for any edge set ''F'' that satisfies <math>|C\cap F|\le |C\setminus F|</math> for every circuit ''C'' of ''G'', there exist <math>|F|</math> pairwise disjoint cuts each containing exactly one element of ''F''. Can we decide in polynomial time whether a graph is Seymour?
